name: What is the difference between commercial remodeling and tenant improvement?

mainEntity.name: Is commercial remodeling the same as tenant improvement construction?
mainEntity.text: Is commercial remodeling the same as tenant improvement construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial remodeling is the umbrella term for improving an existing business property. It can include cosmetic upgrades, structural changes, system replacements, or layout revisions. Tenant improvement is more specific and usually refers to work done to prepare a leased space for a tenant’s operations. That means TI projects often center on floor plans, restrooms, finishes, electrical, HVAC, and code compliance for the new occupant. The distinction matters because landlord responsibilities, lease terms, and permit obligations can differ. Before work starts, owners and tenants should define exactly which items belong to shell delivery and which belong to the tenant improvement scope so there is no confusion about cost or schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commercial remodeling is a broad term for updating a business space, while tenant improvement usually means building out or modifying leased space for a specific occupant. Tenant improvements are a type of commercial remodeling, but not all commercial remodeling is tenant improvement.
